News.title: Trump ‘needs Iraq-style mass invasion plan’ to topple Iran’s terror regime – with hundreds of thousands of troops
News.content:
MORE SHOCK, MORE AWE Trump ‘needs Iraq-style mass invasion plan’ to topple Iran’s terror regime – with hundreds of thousands of troops

DONALD Trump must stage an Iraq-style mass invasion to have any chance of toppling Iran’s regime, an opposition leader has warned.

Mohammad Mohaddessin, who was jailed for daring to oppose rulers, said hundreds of thousands of troops would have to flood Tehran.





Despite Trump‘s rallying cry to Iranians to “take back their country” just hours into the war, the regime is still clinging to power two months on.

The Sun previously told how its “final pillar”, the ruthless Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, will “stop at no crime” to protect the regime.

Activists and analysts alike have warned it will take more than foreign intervention and bombings to put the final nail in the tyranny’s coffin.

Mohaddessin, the president of the Foreign Affairs Committee of the National Council of Resistance of Iran, said Trump would have to deploy a vast number of soldiers deep into enemy territory.

He said given the sheer size of the nation, it would be extremely difficult – if not impossible – to overthrow the regime just through bombings.

Strikes coupled with sanctions weaken it, Mohaddessin added, but would never be enough to spark a revolution.

He told The Sun: “To overthrow the regime, you need soldiers, forces on the ground. If the US wants to overthrow the regime, it needs soldiers on the ground, just as they did in Iraq in 2003.

“The Americans can send a commando team to Tehran for a specific operation, just as they did to rescue a pilot. But they cannot occupy Tehran [with a small number of troops].



“If they want to occupy Tehran, they must send ground troops from the borders all the way to Tehran.

“Tehran is far from Iran’s western borders – 500 to 600km away – and far from its eastern borders – 800 to 900km away – even farther from the southern borders, and a few hundred kilometres from the northern borders.

“Therefore, it is impossible to occupy Iran with a few thousand soldiers.

“Hundreds of thousands of soldiers would be needed to liberate Tehran or to occupy Iran, a country with a population of over 92 million.”

The regime’s future appears to be hanging by a thread following the obliteration of much of its nuclear empire by the US and Israel.



Many of its top brass – including Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei – have also been wiped out.

Iran’s first Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini seized power during the revolution of 1979 – ousting the Shah empire and transforming the state into a theocratic Islamic republic.

His bloody rule was taken over by Khamenei following his death a decade later.

Since then, Tehran has ramped up its nuclear ambitions and become an increasingly bigger threat to not only the Middle East, but the West too.

In a clear sign the regime is bleeding, Khamenei’s heir son Mojtaba has not been seen since he assumed power.



Iran rebels defy internet blackout to reveal they are READY to topple regime Exclusive by Katie Davis, Deputy Foreign Editor BRAVE Iranian rebels have broken through the regime’s internet blackout to tell The Sun: “We are ready to finally take our country back”. Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s grisly downfall that saw him wind up dead in a pile of rubble has left the rogue nation’s repressed public wanting more. One defiant Iranian told me: “The endgame feels real in a way it hasn’t before.” Donald Trump hailed the chief mullah’s pathetic demise after his compound was blitzed as “the single greatest chance for the Iranian people to take back their country”. In a rallying cry to Iran’s population, the US president urged them to seize the opportunity to put the final nail in the nation’s bloodthirsty regime. Courageous Iranians – whose identities we have concealed to protect them – say they are waiting for their moment to finally topple the regime as Khamenei’s inner circle desperately tries to cling to power. Internet blackouts have made it extremely difficult to communicate but, with limited VPN connection, they have managed to share accounts. During January’s deadly protests, when ruthless Khamenei ordered his revolutionary guards to show no mercy, critics told me they would rather die than see his regime survive. But now, months on, the Supreme Leader is dead, and protesters are more certain than ever they could be on the brink of freedom. One 27-year-old rebel living in Tehran told The Sun: “Many of us believed it was possible before, but those uprisings were never meant to be the final chapter by themselves. “The regime survived by hiding behind proxies, money networks, and foreign lobbying. “Now that mask is cracking and their hand is exposed, the endgame feels real in a way it hasn’t before. “It’s a strange mix of relief and iron focus. People are glad to see operations striking terrorists – but the deeper feeling is impatience and readiness. “Everyone is waiting for the moment it becomes our turn to reclaim Iran, and people talk about it out loud now. No more whispers.” READ MORE HERE

Courageous Iranians told The Sun last month they are waiting for their moment to finally end the regime once and for all.

Trump putting boots on the ground inside Iran could spark the final deathblow to the fanatical regime – and inspire an internal uprising.

Mohaddessin said: “You should also take into account the fact that the Iranian people are very patriotic people.

“They are not in favour of their country being occupied.

“Of course, they like and ask for other countries, foreign countries, the US or European countries to support them, but they do not want their country to be occupied.”



The ex-political prisoner said there is a “clear” strategy to overthrow the regime.

He said: “First, public uprising, the uprising of the people. And second, the organised resistance movement, the resistance units within Iran.

“Iranian society is a very, very discontented and volatile society.

“Inflation has reached 75 per cent according to official figures, the highest level of inflation since World War Two.

“And unemployment is somewhere around 25 per cent.



“The Iranian people want freedom; they want democracy. Therefore, a popular uprising is very important and very likely.”

In almost half a century of iron-fist ruling, Iranians have suffered economic hardship, repeated crackdowns – and untold bloodshed, including relentless executions of anyone who dared speak out against the regime.



During January’s bloody protests, up to 40,000 were killed, human rights groups say – while witnesses told The Sun how they saw children gunned down, bodies burnt with acid, and protester’s limbs broken.

Describing themselves as “walking shadows”, they live in fear – and now see a flicker of hope to finally be free from the shackles of the Islamic state.

It comes as more than 1,600 people were executed in the last year in the country’s highest kill count since the post-Iraq war massacre of 1989.

Mohaddessin was himself was jailed after being arrested in 1975 by the Shah’s secret police over his links to the People’s Mojahedin Organisation of Iran (PMOI/MEK).

He was tortured behind bars and after the Islamic regime began its reign of terror and executions in the 1980s, he was forced into exile and fled to Paris.



“As long as this regime exists, they cannot put aside torture, execution, pressure on the people because the existence of the regime, the survival of the regime, is based on two elements,” Mohaddessin added.

“First, suppression inside Iran, execution and other forms of, other kinds of suppression.

“Second, to export terrorism and fundamentalism and warmongering behind of its borders.

“The best solution to decrease the level of executions is some kind of international condemnation, international punishment to the regime, who massacred 120,000 political prisoners in the last decades, including outside Iran.”

Floating hospitals, hovercrafts & drone lasers: Trump’s force ready to raid islands Exclusive by Katie Davis WARSHIPS the size of football fields equipped with hospitals and drone lasers have been deployed as Donald Trump gears up to seize Iran’s key islands. Thousands of marines have been arriving in the war-torn region as the US president mulls whether to unleash a ground invasion. The Sun told how plans had been drawn up for Trump’s 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit to storm vital island fortresses to unlock the Strait of Hormuz. But now the Pentagon has given its clearest sign yet of invasion intentions after ordering prefabricated bunkers for island occupations, sources say. Guarded by ruthless IRGC agents armed to the teeth, insiders have warned wrestling these islands from Iran’s grip could be an extremely bloody battle. IRGC island garrisons, gunboats and naval drones are so far being decimated by bunker-busting air bombardments as well as low-flying Apache helicopters and A-10 Thunderbolt jets. But marines – trained to seize and fortify small islands – could encounter intense barrages of Iranian missiles and killer drones launched from virtually anywhere on Iran’s mainland. Iran’s parliament speaker, ex-IRGC officer Bagher Ghalibaf, previously threatened to “rain down fire” on any invading US forces. US Army War College professor Evan Ellis told The Sun: “Marines could become a drone magnet.” Additional Marine Expeditionary Units (MEU) with logistical support vessels are now on the way from bases in California to bolster any capture efforts – putting muscle on Trump’s threat to capture Kharg. The 11th Amphibious Ready Group with the landing dock support vessels and 2,500 Marines was sent to join the 31st MEU, with the same number of troops already on station around the Hormuz on USS Tripoli. Reinforcements were due to arrive in the Middle East theatre – including a converted container ship equipped with an on board hospital of more than 100 beds. Large numbers of wounded are expected in what could be a “dangerous” mission to gain control of the world’s main oil shipping lands being choked by the IRGC. READ MORE HERE

It comes as Tehran’s Revolutionary Guards opened fire at vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz yesterday in a major re-escalation that has tested the fragile two-week ceasefire.



And Trump has warned that US forces will have to “start dropping bombs again” if Iran does not concede to Washington‘s demands to give up its stash of highly-enriched uranium.

Iran has doubled down on its pledge to restrict ships passing through the waterway as long as the US blockade of Iranian ports remains in place.

Mediators are now scrambling to secure further talks before the ceasefire expires this week.

The fragile ceasefire in place between the US and Iran is due to run out by Wednesday.

Iran on Saturday said it had received new proposals from the US, and Pakistani mediators were working to arrange another round of direct negotiations.



But Mohaddessin believes there is one overriding reason why Iran is resisting deals tabled.

“The regime has a very simple calculation regarding the war,” he said.

“They say the US cannot overthrow the regime through bombing, they are very certain of this.

“Second, they believe that if they accept the US’ conditions – or at least a significant portion of them – this will lead to a certain amount of chaos within the regime and weaken it from within.

“And it paves the way for a very powerful uprising. The regime’s leaders fear this scenario. They are also under great pressure because of the war.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“For example, if they give up their nuclear ambitions, tomorrow people within the regime – not just the Iranian people – will say to the leaders: Why did we spend so much money, why have we paid such a price?

“So chaos will begin within the regime.”

News.title: ‘Firebomb thrown through window’ of London synagogue in fifth arson attack on Jewish property in a month
News.content:
ARSON PROBE ‘Firebomb thrown through window’ of London synagogue in fifth arson attack on Jewish property in a month

A “FIREBOMB” has reportedly been thrown through the window of a synagogue in the fifth antisemitic arson attack in a month.

The incident saw the place of worship in Kenton, north-west London, suffer smoke damage after it was targeted in a yet another attack.



An object is understood to have been thrown through one of the building’s windows, landing in an internal room, according to the Community Security Trust (CST).



Police and fire crews were scrambled to the scene last night after the incident was reported to emergency services.

A cordon has been set up around the place of worship today as emergency crews continue to work at the scene.

Forensic officers have been seen at the synagogue as an investigation into the latest antisemitic arson incident gets underway.

No injuries or significant structural damage have been reported as a result of the attempted attack.



An internal room of the building is understood to have suffered some minor smoke damage in the attack, however.

Officers on the scene were spotted searching a black SUV near the Kenton United Synagogue, which sits near a school, as they probed the incident today.

A spokesperson for the CST said: “We are aware of another attempted arson, this time targeting a synagogue in north London, following similar recent incidents targeting the Jewish community in Finchley, Golders Green and Hendon.

“On this occasion there was minor smoke damage to an internal room, but there were no injuries and no significant structural damage.



“We want to thank the Met Police and London Fire Brigade for responding quickly and for all they are doing to protect the Jewish community during this unprecedented period.

“We are supporting the affected location and are working closely with the police as they investigate and seek to identify those responsible.

“We urge people to remain vigilant and to report any suspicious activity, at any time of day or night, to the police immediately on 999 and then to CST.”



The CST monitors antisemitism and provides protection for Jewish communities in the UK.

Last night’s incident marks the fifth antisemitic arson attack to unfold in just a month after four Jewish ambulances were torched in an attack by masked arsonists.

Six fire engines and around 40 firefighters raced to the scene in Golders Green just before 1.45am on March 23 as the blaze took hold of the vehicles.

Shocking CCTV footage of the incident appears to show three masked yobs setting the ambulances alight before scarpering into the night.

More recently an attempted arson attack unfolded at a synagogue in Finchley shortly after midnight.



Two balaclava-clad people threw two bottles and a brick at the Finchley Reform Synagogue, in London on April 15 – Holocaust Remembrance Day in Israel.

On the same day, a Persian Language media organisation in north west London was targeted in an arson attack.

And, in Hendon, two days later, another attack is being probed by counter-terror cops after a Jewish business in North London was targeted.

A man was seen approaching the row of shops in Hendon with a plastic bag which he placed next to the buildings and set on fire, cops said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The attack on the synagogue last night now marks the fifth arson incident to unfold in north-west London in just a month.



The Sun has contacted the Met Police and London Fire Brigade for comment.

News.title: Gut-wrenching ‘K-cramps’ & families destroyed by 14-year-old addicts… the ketamine ‘choke hold’ gripping trendy UK city
News.content:
HUNDREDS of students bask in the spring sunshine on an inner-city green chatting, laughing and looking like they don’t have a care in the world.

Indeed, many of them are looking forward to bright futures, but there’s a more sinister force at work in a city that ranks among the most blighted by ketamine addiction in Europe – with the drug locally called ‘Bristol Crystal’.





More residue of the illicit drug has been found in the wastewater of Bristol over weekends than any other city on the continent, new multi-city data from the European Union Drugs Agency shows.

Seemingly happy, a young woman sits with fellow students on a park bench in College Green, which is heaving with throngs of teenagers during lunch break.

But, as she confesses to The Sun, getting her degree is the least of her worries, being one of the many who have succumbed to ketamine addiction.



Lottie (not her real name), 20, says the new figures come as “no surprise”, adding: “Ketamine is an evil drug which is billed as not being as dangerous as other drugs and most people at uni are using.

“At school we’re taught about the dangers of crack, heroin and (crystal) meth, but not about the damage ket can do, or the deep level of addiction you can have.

“I first took it at 14, as my older brother was into drugs and gave me some. I used it casually, maybe every few weekends, which became once a week and then every day.

“By the age of 16 I was in a bit of a choke hold. Since then, I don’t think I’ve been a week without it.



“The more you take, the more you need to get the disassociated feeling it gives you.

“I get three lines out of a gram, and it’s cheaper and more readily available in Bristol than it is in London, where it’s like 7g for £50. In Bristol you can get 10g for £50.”

Lottie – who, with perfectly applied make-up, looks nothing like the stereotypical image of an addict – is desperate to warn others to steer clear of the drug.



She says: “I’m a functioning addict, so I still attend lectures and manage with my work, but ketamine is ruining my life and my health.

“Usually my bladder is fine, but if I drink, I have to go for a wee every ten minutes. The worst thing is the K-cramps it gives me, which happens to my kidneys, stomach and gallbladder. It feels like a hydraulic press.

“Sometimes at festivals I’ve had my drugs checked and been told they’re being mixed with other drugs like M-Kat (Mephadrone) or speed.”

Mixing stimulants like speed with depressants, like ketamine, is extremely dangerous, putting a massive strain on the heart and central nervous system. It can lead to cardiac arrest and heart attacks.

Lottie adds: “I get support from the Bristol Drugs Project, but I’m addicted to the disassociation. If I stop, I have to feel everything I haven’t been feeling.



“It would be easier to name the people who don’t do it than those who do.

“A few years ago, dealers mostly offered cocaine, but ketamine has become the main drug now – if you asked for cocaine, they’d probably only have ket because of the amount of people wanting it.

“I’ve been in hospital three times because of the K-cramps and low heart rate, lost friends and my family because they have lost hope for me. I’m scared for my generation. If I knew what I know now, I would never have taken it in the first place.”

In the wastewater survey of 130 cities, Bristol recorded a peak weekend average of 350.18 micrograms of ketamine residue per 1,000 people – more than the likes of Amsterdam or Berlin.

While experts have cautioned that wastewater studies are not a definitive measure, the findings are certainly damning, with Bristol also ranking second in Europe for the amount of cocaine measured – behind only Middlesborough.



It comes after The Sun also revealed the city was facing a growing crisis with homelessness, with rough sleepers resigned to sleeping in tents and even caves, while its renowned Georgian houses are snapped up for millions of pounds.

Used as a horse tranquiliser and in paediatric medicine as an anaesthetic, unprescribed ketamine use in the UK has increased eight-fold since 2015, according to the Health Department.

Another college source we spoke with said he was aware of the rapid increase in popularity of the Class B drug, also known as Special K.

“It’s something the university is known for having an issue with, especially with the first years in the halls,” he told The Sun.

“If you go to a party there’s usually ketamine being taken openly, most people don’t even try to hide it because it’s not seen as being such a big deal as what people might commonly refer to as harder drugs.”



With the right help and support, many people can kick their addiction to ket, which comes as a crystalline powder or a liquid which has hallucinogenic effects.

One 18-year-old tells how he had been addicted to ket for eight months while he was 15 and still at school.

He says: “There was a period after my parents split that I struggled emotionally and I started drinking but then went to a party where someone offered me ket.



“I loved how it blocked out my problems, numbed how I was feeling, and started using it all the time. I’d have it before school, during school and after school. All day long.

“But my friends pulled me up on it when they suspected it was a problem. By then it had started to hurt when I peed, and I knew if I kept going, I could have serious bladder problems which might be irreversible.

“I intentionally weaned myself off it, with support from my family. It was really hard, probably the toughest thing I’ve ever had to do. Sometimes I’m desperate for the feeling it gave me, but so far, I’ve managed to stay strong enough to resist.”

Chronic use of ket has exploded so much in Bristol, particularly between 16–24-year-olds, that Southmead Hospital has seen a sharp rise in cases who are seen in its Functional Urology clinic in the Bristol Urological Institute.

It damages the lining of the bladder and can shrink it, and in some cases people as young as 19 have needed major surgery.



GETTING HELP: If you think that you have a drug addiction then please contact your GP. You can also visit FRANK for honest information about drugs and to find local treatment services. If you are having trouble finding the right help, call the FRANK drugs helpline on 03001236600 Or click here to visit the NHS website for more advice and support

Common symptoms of damage are pain, a feeling of needing to urinate urgently or very frequently, passing blood in urine and leaking urine.

‘K cramps’ are related to the bowel. Patients experience bladder and urethral pain due to the inflammation caused by ketamine and may also experience a ‘spasm-like’ pain from the bladder.

If there is irreversible damage, patients will require major surgery to either augment the bladder using part of the bowel or remove the bladder altogether and install a stoma bag.

Bladder damage can can also cause infections, bleeding, blockages and incontinence.

Deaths involving ketamine have increased 20-fold since 2014, with 37 deaths recorded in England and Wales in 2023.



In 2024 an inquest concluded an unnamed young man from Bristol died from ketamine toxicity, and his mother has since campaigned to raise awareness of the dangers of the drug. The total number of deaths in Bristol is unknown.

A spokesperson for the University of the West of England said: “We’ve had a harm reduction policy in place at UWE Bristol since 2018, which means we take a proactive approach to educating our students on the risks of drug and alcohol use.

“Working collaboratively with our Students’ Union and education charity SOS UK, we have run targeted campaigns over a number of years specifically about ketamine use.

“This includes tailored resources for students, pop-up information stands and engagement events to listen to and support students, so they can make informed decisions about drug use.



“Students can self-refer to our drugs and alcohol service where they are given solutions-focused support with face-to-face appointments in a non-judgemental environment.”

A University of Bristol spokesperson said: “Here at the University of Bristol we focus on minimising risks from using drugs and alcohol by supporting students to make informed decisions.

“We regularly provide them with information about the risks, how they might reduce potential harms and where they can go for help and support if they need it. We work closely with local drug services, Avon and Somerset Police and Bristol City Council to keep our students safe.

“This does not mean anti-social or criminal behaviour is acceptable and such misconduct will continue to be addressed robustly through our disciplinary regulations. Any student found to be involved in the supply of illegal drugs will be referred to the University’s police officer.”

Superintendent Steph McKenna, Avon and Somerset’s drugs lead, said: “It is widely recognised the serious harm illegal drugs, such as ketamine, can cause.



“For that reason, we work closely with council public health teams and key partners – such as the Bristol Combatting Drugs Partnership (CDP) – to help keep the public safe.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“A number of arrests have been made in recent years of people being found in possession of ketamine. In many cases those individuals have been charged and brought before the courts, but in some instances for lower-level offences it’s felt a more productive way forward is an educational one as that can lead to better long-term outcomes.

“Ultimately, our main focus is about stopping ketamine reaching people in the first place, which is why we would place greater emphasis on targeting drug suppliers who are profiteering from the misery drugs cause. We have successfully been able to bring a number of such offenders to justice in recent years and will continue to do so.”

News.title: Rat poison found inside jar of HiPP baby food after recall from 1,500 supermarkets in Austria as cops probe foul play
News.content:
POISON ALERT Rat poison found inside jar of HiPP baby food after recall from 1,500 supermarkets in Austria as cops probe foul play

RAT poison has been found inside a jar of HiPP baby food in Austria after an urgent recall.

The shocking discovery comes after the product was recalled from 1,500 supermarkets over safety fears.





A sample from one of the recalled jars of “Carrots and Potatoes” baby food tested positive for rat poison, police in Burgenland, Austria, said.

HiPP said the jars may have been tampered with.

It could not be ruled out that a dangerous substance was introduced into the product, the company said.

Consuming the contents of jars could be life-threatening, HiPP warned.

Cops said affected jars were marked with a white sticker and a red circle on the bottom.

A missing safety seal, or an unusual smell could also be signs the jar has been interfered with.

Jars seized by police in the Czech Republic and Slovakia have also been found to contain a toxic substance.

The police also said authorities in Austria were warned about the risk following investigations in Germany.



HiPP said: “According to our current knowledge, this critical situation involves an external criminal interference that affects the SPAR Austria distribution channel.”

Austria’s agency for food protection said the poison may have been introduced as part of an extortion scheme.

A SPAR spokesperson said the product recall was a precautionary measure affecting 1,500 stores in Austria, with no impact on outlets elsewhere.

Jars sold in Eurospar, Interspar and Maximarkt shops also fall under the recall.

SPAR and HiPP advised customers not to consume the contents of the jars bought from SPAR Austria.



They said customers would receive a full refund on returned products.

Police advised customers to wash hands thoroughly if they came into contact with a jar.

Several similar food scares have hit the baby food market recently.

In February, dozens of children fell ill with food poisoning after consuming baby formula contaminated with a dangerous toxin.

Food giant Nestle recalled more than 60 batches of formula suspected to contain cereulide.



The toxin is produced by some strains of the bacteria Bacillus cereus and can cause food poisoning symptoms – like severe vomiting and diarrhoea.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) announced that at least 36 children had gotten suspected food poisoning from contaminated baby formula.

Twenty-four were reported in England, seven in Scotland, three in Wales, one in the North of Ireland, and one from the Crown Dependencies.

News.title: Mystery as bodies of 50 babies and six adults found dumped in cemetery as cops probe ‘illegal burial’
News.content:
DISTURBING FIND Mystery as bodies of 50 babies and six adults found dumped in cemetery as cops probe ‘illegal burial’

A GRIM mass grave filled with the bodies of 50 babies and six adults has been discovered in a cemetery.

The death pit was uncovered by cops in Cumuto, Trinidad and Tobago on Saturday.





Initial investigations suggest the corpses were illegally disposed of, but the full circumstances remain a mystery.

The bodies of the adults are those of two women and four men, according to local media.

Five of the adult corpses were found with toe tags, used for identification in morgues.

Two also showed signs that autopsies had been carried out.



Evidence is now being collected and the origin of the remains is being investigated.

“The nature of this discovery is deeply disturbing, and we understand the emotional impact it will have on the families and the entire community,” Police Chief Allister Guevarro told the Trinidad Express.

“Every body must be treated with dignity and in accordance with the law.

“Any person or institution that has violated this duty will be held fully accountable.”



He said police were treating the case “with urgency, sensitivity and unwavering commitment to uncovering the truth.”

Two men, aged 18 and 25, have been detained by cops.

They were employed by a funeral home and claim they had been tasked with digging a grave for a burial for the poor.

According to police, the two men said they had disposed of several bodies including those of babies at the site.

It comes after a mass grave filled with dozens of dead bodies was unearthed in Serbia.



Archaeologists believe those found in the mass burial site may have been fleeing an attack on their village nearly 3,000 years ago.

A team of researchers made the chilling discovery after re-examining remains found in an area of land at Gomalva, which also included eerie “animal offerings”.

The grave was originally discovered in the early 70s, with researchers reporting women and children were targeted in the killings that took place around 800BC.

Barry Molloy, associate professor at University College Dublin wrote in the Nature Human Behaviour journal that the team were “expecting a village community that all died when a disease came along”.

However, he said the evidence now points to an ancient genocide.



Researchers discovered some of those found in the pit had fractured skulls while a few bore marks on their bones from arrows, spears or swords.

Most displayed no signs of trauma, which researchers believe points to extremely violent episodes between competing groups.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Not only had the bodies not been stripped of their valuables, offerings were made in what must have been a respectful ritual,” wrote Molloy.

“There’s clearly a choice being made about who’s being killed.”

News.title: Two children rushed to hospital after horror crash with police car in quiet seaside town
News.content:
SMASH HORROR Two children rushed to hospital after horror crash with police car in quiet seaside town

TWO children have been rushed to hospital after a horror crash with a police car in a quiet seaside town.

The collision occurred in Maryport, Cumbria, on Saturday evening and involved two children of secondary school age, police said.



Cumbria Police said one victim was raced to hospital with serious injuries and is in a critical but stable condition.



The other child suffered minor injuries and has since been discharged from hospital.

At the time of the collision, the police vehicle was “not in pursuit or responding to an emergency incident”.

Senhouse Street remained closed on Saturday as an investigation was launched.

The police force has now referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

Anyone with information or dash cam footage of the incident is urged to get in touch with the force.

Superintendent Sarah Jones, Cumbria Constabulary said: “Our thoughts are with the two young people involved in this incident and their families.

“Officers are continuing to carry out enquiries to fully understand the circumstances, and we would encourage anyone with information to come forward.”

News.title: Hunt for man who ‘exposed himself’ to mum & young child from bushes before doing same thing hours later to lone woman
News.content:
COP PROBE Hunt for man who ‘exposed himself’ to mum & young child from bushes before doing same thing hours later to lone woman

A CYCLIST allegedly exposed himself to a woman and her young child before doing the same thing to a lone woman later the same day.

Cops are now frantically hunting for a suspect after both of the harrowing incidents, which occurred in Oxford, Oxfordshire, on Wednesday, were reported.



The first incident saw a man reportedly pass a woman and her young child on his bike before dismounting and going into some nearby bushes.

He then exposed himself to the woman and her child from the bushes, cops say.



Later the same day a man cycled past a lone woman before dismounting his bike and entering some nearby bushes.

In an identical incident to the first alleged offence, he then exposed himself to the second victim from the bushes, cops say.

Thames Valley Police is now hunting for a suspect described as a black man in his twenties with a thin build.

He had afro style hair and was wearing dark jeans and a dark top and was cycling on a black bike.

The first of the two incidents is alleged to have occurred on the path near Longford Way at around 11:20am.

The second reportedly happened on the cycle track between Hagbourne and Upton at about 1pm.

Cops are now appealing for anyone who may have information, CCTV or door-cam footage that could assist their investigation to come forward.

Investigating officer, PC Daniel Mellor, said: “I am appealing to anybody who witnessed either of these incidents, or may have information that could assist in our investigation to contact Thames Valley Police.



“I am also appealing to anyone else who may have been in the area, walking along this lane or anyone nearby with CCTV or door-cam footage.

“Officers have gathered the details of some witnesses at the time of the report but are looking for any further witnesses or information.

“Anyone with information can call 101 or make report via our website, quoting reference number 43260182552.

“Alternatively, for anonymity, you can call the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: The ‘runaway heiress’ swindler who fooled me out of £1MILLION with box of cruel tricks – before vanishing into thin air
News.content:
A SELF-MADE woman who had worked tirelessly since she was 15, Bridget Hutchcroft had built an enviable life for herself in a trendy corner of west London.

To her horror, however, all that was to come crashing down in a swindle worthy of a Netflix drama. Before Bridget knew it, a woman now dubbed the ‘runaway heiress’ had walked away with £1million of her life-savings – with the shop owner now telling The Sun of her astonishing fight to get her money back, as mystery swirls over the Gucci-clad stranger.



The baffling tale began one day as Bridget worked in her Knightsbridge clothes shop, only to be greeted by an unmistakable figure clad in designer clothes and walking two Italian greyhounds.

Despite originally dismissing her as “rude”, the 66-year-old found herself being succored in by Bentley-driving Ekaterina Barrett.



Walking her Italian greyhounds, wearing a purple Gucci dress, clutching designer handbags and with fiery red hair, Barrett, now 69, was an unmistakable and familiar sight in London’s most exclusive neighbourhoods.

Bridget, meanwhile, had been running the Pandora Dress Agency, a shop specialising in second-hand designer clothes, but was at her most vulnerable after suffering a crippling breakdown.

And heartbreakingly, this is when she says her new “friend” Barrett – since widely dubbed the “runaway heiress” after Bridget went public with her case – pounced.

But Barrett’s background as an “heiress” is as opaque as her designer shades.

And she is now believed to hunkered down in Monaco.



Bridget accuses the socialite of swindling her out of more than a million pounds after she gave her a loan which was never paid back.

But not wanting to be defeated, the stalwart shop owner has been locked in a long-running legal battle over the funds.

“I’m not gonna let some rich woman take my money off me, taking advantage of my kindness and generosity when I was seriously ill,” Bridget told The Sun.

Years of wrangling has raged over the money, with the High Court ruling in 2022 that Barrett owes Bridget £1.6million including costs and interest over unpaid loans obtained through “fraudlent misrepresentation”.

She was also handed a four-month suspended sentence in 2024 for lying under oath and submitting fake documents, and ordered to pay a £100,000 fine.



Bridget says “calculated” Barrett capitalised on her vulnerable state and kind nature – with her barrister telling the High Court the socialite “took advantage” of the shop owner.

Barrett has denied being a fraudster – claiming in court the payments were for designer clothes, not borrowed cash.

“I’m not paying back a penny,” she reportedly declared when previously confronted by reporters.

I had seen her wearing designer dresses which cost £40,000, so it never crossed my mind that I would not get paid back at some point, and saw myself doing a favour to help a friend Bridget Hutchcroft

The pair met in 2017 when Ukrainian-born Barrett first waltzed into Pandora Dress Agency, a treasure trove of designer fashion tucked just around the corner from Harrods.

The boutique is a cornerstone of high society style and has attracted a dazzling clientele over the decades, including the late Diana, Catherine Zeta-Jones and Hollywood icon Ava Gardner.



Rails are packed with high-end brands such as Gucci, Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Versace and Prada pieces, drawing fashion lovers from across the world.

At the time they met, Barrett appeared to be living the dream.

She was based in a plush £4.2million Mayfair flat, swept through London in a Bentley and dazzled in couture outfits worth tens of thousands.

Though initially the pair did not hit it off, with Bridget finding the woman “rude” and “irritating”, things soon changed.

When one day Barrett asked animal-loving Bridget if she would look after her two Italian Greyhounds, Luca and Louis, it marked the beginning of their unlikely bond.



“I was recovering from a breakdown, I really had not been well,” Bridget told The Sun.

“And walking the dogs was very calming, it was like therapy for me. I have always loved animals and it didn’t really seem that big of a chore.”



Fast forward a couple of months and the pair had grown closer through regular dog walks.

Then came the turning point.

Barrett told Bridget she needed to borrow money while she was dealing with a divorce.

Bridget said: “I had no reason to believe that she wouldn’t pay me back.

“I had seen her Mayfair apartment, she would drive around in a Bentley, would always be wearing incredibly flashy designer clothes and would always gloat about recent buys, travels, and where she had been and what she had been up to.



“I had seen her wearing designer dresses which cost £40,000, so it never crossed my mind that I would not get paid back at some point, and I saw myself doing a favour to help a friend.

“I lent the money because I am nice. And I thought she was good for it, I had no reason to think otherwise.”

She didn’t wish to come clean about what had happened. Barrett had so much control and influence over her Roger Slater

Before long, Bridget realised she had loaned more than £1million.

“I clearly wasn’t well,” Bridget said.

“No sane person would answer the phone to somebody asking for some £200,000 and say ‘yes, no worries, I will get that sent across shortly’.”



Bridget had been battling with her mental health for a number of years.

It was only after confiding in her shop manager Sona that alarm bells truly rang. Sona contacted Bridget’s life-long friend Roger Slater, who stepped in.

Roger told The Sun: “I couldn’t believe it. Without any other choice and of course concerned, I confronted Bridget about it.”

Pulling no punches, Roger blasted Barrett as a “hyena” and said he “had to help”.



Bridget and Roger went to police but were told it was a civil matter.

“I worked for everything I’ve got since the age of 15,” said Bridget, who grew up in a working-class household in Stalybridge in Greater Manchester.

“I have moved on and put it all behind me. I did not really have the time to sit around crying.

“I had to get on with it and go to work. Ekaterina has nothing but the dogs. That is all she puts her love into.

“And I was determined to not let her get away with this.”



With no other option, Bridget instructed lawyers and launched a High Court claim.

She was warned that even if she won, there was no guarantee she would recover the money.

Bridget told the court that, when asked to repay the loan, her former friend said: “If you do not wait for me to repay the loans in my own time, you will have to wait for one hundred years.”



Roger and Bridget launched the battle to reclaim the money. Barrett fought back by counter-suing, claiming Bridget actually owed her money in relation to designer clothes.

The dispute landed in the High Court, where Bridget accused her former friend of “fraudulent misrepresentation”.

She claimed Barrett had posed as a multi-millionaire to secure the loans.

In October 2022, a judge ruled firmly in Bridget’s favour and ordered Barrett to repay more than £1.6million including interest.



Despite the judgment, the money was not returned.

The case returned to court in June 2023 as Bridget’s legal team tried to pin down Barrett’s finances.

Barrett insisted she was not wealthy and claimed her lifestyle was funded entirely by her family.

Her opponents said that was simply not true and pointed to her links to a luxury Monaco property known as Saint Andre.

The legal war took an extraordinary turn in 2024.



LEGAL WARFARE

Barrett produced what she claimed was a settlement agreement showing the debt had been reduced to £800,000.

But the High Court found the document was forged.

A judge ruled the signature was not Bridget’s and concluded Barrett had been responsible for creating the fake document.

Barrett was held in contempt of court – and given a four-month suspended sentence.

The sentence was suspended due to her poor health and the fact she cares for her mother, who is in her 90s.



During the judge’s sentencing remarks, she was seen blowing kisses – for which she was blasted by the judge, Mrs Justice Heather Williams.

Despite years of hearings, explosive claims and damning rulings, the fight is still not over.

Bridget continues her battle to recover the fortune she says was taken from her by the woman she once thought she trusted.

Barrett’s whereabouts still remain unknown – as does the true nature of her apparent wealth.

The Sun has attempted to contact Barrett through her lawyers but has had no response.

News.title: Harrow synagogue 'firebombed' as London faces 'terrifying daily arson attacks'
News.content:
Harrow synagogue 'firebombed' as London faces 'terrifying daily arson attacks'

An investigation has been launched after Kenton United Synagogue in Harrow was allegedly 'firebombed' on Saturday, following other reported attacks on Jewish property in north-west London

View 3 Images Police officers at the scene near the Kenton United Synagogue in Harrow (Image: Jamie Lashmar/PA Wire)

Police have launched an investigation after a synagogue was allegedly "firebombed" last night.

‌



Multiple arson or attempted arson attacks have been reported on Jewish property in north-west London in the past month.

‌



The incident at Kenton United Synagogue in Harrow on Saturday night caused minor smoke damage to an internal room but no injuries or significant structural damage, the Community Security Trust (CST) said.

‌



The building is close to a school and children’s playground, and police were seen searching a black SUV nearby on Sunday morning.

A large cordon is in place and a forensics officer, fire investigation dogs and several plainclothes officers were working at the scene. One marked and five unmarked police cars were outside the place of worship.

View 3 Images Multiple arson or attempted arson attacks have been reported on Jewish property in north-west London in the past month (Image: Toby Shepheard / Story Picture Agency)

‌



Dead bodies of at least 50 babies found dumped in Trinidad and Tobago graveyard READ MORE :

A spokesperson for the CST, the charity which monitors antisemitism and provides protection for Jewish communities in the UK, said: “We are aware of another attempted arson, this time targeting a synagogue in north London, following similar recent incidents targeting the Jewish community in Finchley, Golders Green and Hendon.

“On this occasion there was minor smoke damage to an internal room, but there were no injuries and no significant structural damage.

“We want to thank the Met Police and London Fire Brigade for responding quickly and for all they are doing to protect the Jewish community during this unprecedented period.

‌



“We are supporting the affected location and are working closely with the police as they investigate and seek to identify those responsible.

View 3 Images A large police cordon is in place (Image: Jamie Lashmar/PA Wire)

“We urge people to remain vigilant and to report any suspicious activity, at any time of day or night, to the police immediately on 999 and then to CST.”

Article continues below

"We are supporting the affected location and are working closely with the police as they investigate and seek to identify those responsible.”

A Campaign Against Antisemitism spokesperson said: "Last night, another Jewish synagogue in London was firebombed, this time in Kenton. Thankfully, the damage was limited." They added that this “is now terrifyingly becoming a spate of daily arson attacks on the Jewish community”.

News.title: Get the same medication for a lower price by checking hidden code
News.content:
Get the same medication for a lower price by checking hidden code

People could be paying less for the exact same product - just in different packaging

View 2 Images People should double check before buying their next pack of pills (Image: Getty)

Anyone buying pain relief medication should check for an easy-to-ignore code on the box that might mean nothing to the untrained eye. But experts have suggested that it could be the key to avoiding getting "ripped off" by bold claims.

‌



Posting on Instagram, an MSE spokesperson claimed that "drug companies are ripping [people] off" for their period pain relief. Taking a closer look beyond what the packaging claims can sometimes reveal a cheaper option - even if it claims to be for a completely different body part.

‌



They said: "When the cramps hit, you might reach for period pain relief tablets, because something specific should work better, right? But, that pain-specific branding is often marketing bull.

‌



"A lot of the time, migraine tablets, period pain and back pain medications are literally the same thing, just in different packaging and with wildly different price tags."

If people want to find the same medication for less, look for the PL code printed on the box. This is the license number for a particular drug manufactured by a specific manufacturer and matching numbers between products only means one thing - it's the "exact same medicine".

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The MSE video showed one example of a popular brand for managing period pain, Feminax Express (sold in Boots for £5.40), which had the same code as Boots' own-brand migraine pain relief tablets (worth £2.89). Both tablets contain the same doses of ibuprofen lysine (342mg).

"If these two PL numbers are the same, it's the same drug, no matter what the front of the box claims. So, now you know, don't let them rip you off."

The only difference usually between these pills or tablets is the colours used in the capsule, and the fact that they are marketed for different conditions (sometimes only slightly). The MSE website claimed that, while this seems a little underhanded, medicine companies are allowed to have these 'informative' names on the packet to help you choose the product you need.

‌



View 2 Images The common period pain medicine had the same code as a Boots-own migraine solution (Image: Getty)

In other medication news, people who take statins have been reminded of a common drink they should try to avoid at all costs. Combining statins with this juice could make them more powerful and even “toxic”.

Approximately eight million people in the UK are estimated to be prescribed statins. These medicines help reduce levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (or "bad" cholesterol) in the bloodstream.

Article continues below

While statins could therefore prove life-saving, using them carries their own hazards. Read the full story here.

News.title: Inside Passport Photo Service: Incredible never-before-seen celebrity portraits revealed
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Inside Passport Photo Service: Incredible never-before-seen celebrity portraits revealed

Passport Photo Service: An Unexpected Archive of Celebrity Portraits features 300 never-before-seen celebrity images from its archive, from Mick Jagger to Arnold Schwarzenegger

View 7 Images Legendary boxer Muhammad Ali (Image: AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin)

When an ex-boxer overheard an angry American’s gripes about being unable to get a passport photo in time to fly home the next day, he had a lightbulb moment. David Sharkey had been honing his photographic skills since the late 1940s, when he sold his ration books and bought a Leica camera, becoming a ‘smudge,’ snapping tourists in London’s Trafalgar Square. The derogatory moniker came from complaints when tourists failed to receive their photos and were allegedly told by errant lensmen that their addresses had been ‘smudged’ in the rain.

‌



But there would be none of that in David’s new venture. It was 1953 and, spotting a gap in the market, after his encounter with the angry man from the US in Wolfe’s Coffee House in the West End, quicker than you could say ‘cheese,’ he’d set up Express Photos on Oxford Street.

‌



Moving in 1957 to number 449 under the new name, Passport Photo Service, it was bang opposite Selfridges and less than a minute’s walk from the US, Canadian and Japanese embassies. The prime site provided plenty of trade from people seeking passport photos, visas and green cards.

‌



7 View 7 Images David Sharkey had been honing his photographic skills since the late 1940s, when he sold his ration books and bought a Leica camera, becoming a ‘smudge,’ snapping tourists in London’s Trafalgar Square (Image: Supplied) 7 View 7 Images Philip Sharkey (centre) with photographers Ivo Carmo (left) and Piotr Gorka (right), outside 39 North Row (Image: Philip Sharkey)

And during the 66 years the business operated as a family venture - finally closing in 2019 - more than 800 of its thousands of customers were celebrities, stars of the stage, screen and sport. Now a new book - Passport Photo Service: An Unexpected Archive of Celebrity Portraits - by the son of the photo shop’s founder, Philip Sharkey, who joined the business aged 16, features 300 never-before-seen celebrity images from its archive.

The first photo service in London promising to be “ready in 10 minutes,” David made the venture a family affair. Himself a former East End boxer, he was married to Ann, a professional dancer, who quit to become the receptionist; while her brother, Peter, joined their ranks when he was just 15 - and Philip entered the family firm, aged 16, in 1973.

‌



View 7 Images Pictured: Muhammad Ali. Boxer, 11 June 1974. Signed with a dedication to Philip Sharkey (Image: Philip Sharkey)

Cited above the ground floor, so not immediately visible, they used sandwich board men, who walked up and down Oxford Street advertising them in all weathers. Philip, 68, says: “We had never missed a day of trading, not even when the IRA bombed Selfridges in December 1974.” Every country had its own specifications and rules regarding passport and visa photos and they catered to them all, diligently taking and developing photos in what had once been Arts and Crafts movement pioneer William Morris’s workshop.

Philip remembers one customer’s disbelief when he saw the shop’s wall of fame, where they mounted frames filled with celebrity images. The man exclaimed: “Muhammad Ali, Joan Collins, Mick Jagger, Arnold Schwarzenegger, I don’t believe you’ve photographed all these famous people!”

‌



View 7 Images Sean Connery, pictured on September 1977 (Image: Philip Sharkey)

Philip had become used to such protestations. He recalls: “One ordinary Saturday in 1987, a customer was scrutinizing the three large frames full of celebrity passport photos that hung on the wall. Tutting and shaking his head, he - like other customers before him - expressed disbelief that they had all come to us. A lady in her early 60s, dressed casually and sporting a large pair of glasses, replied ‘well, everybody needs a passport, so they have to have somewhere to go to be photographed. After the gentleman had left, Ava Gardner looked up at me with a smile. ‘I don’t think I convinced him,’ she said.’”

Philip’s book is like a social history, with stars from Madonna, and Mick Jagger to Angelina Jolie, Sean Connery, Kate Winslet, Tilda Swinton, Alex Guinness, Marty Feldman, Dudley Moore and David Hockney all featured. He laughs, recalling a visit from famous cutlery bender, Uri Geller, who bent the studio spoon, saying: “We didn’t ask him to. It was our only spoon.”

‌



View 7 Images Actor Dudley Moore, pictured on 30 November 1967 (Image: Philip Sharkey)

Described as feeling like “a special kind of club,” by Stephen Fry, some of the studio’s photos are particularly thought-provoking. Take the passport photo of Nancy Spungen, snapped on 10 August, 1978. The American girlfriend of Sex Pistols star Sid Vicious, she was found dead in the couple’s bathroom at New York’s Chelsea Hotel - stabbed in the abdomen - aged just 20, on 12 October. Vicious was charged with her murder, but died of a heroin overdose while on bail in February 1979, aged 21.

Philip says: “Sid Vicious’s girlfriend came in for what would be her last passport photo. Tragically, she was killed two months later. She was originally wearing a badge that read ‘I’m a McLaren puppet’ which I suggested she take off for her photo.”

‌



Of the great and the good who posed for the Passport Photo Service, one of the most memorable was undoubtedly Muhammad Ali, in 1974. Philip says he “stopped by on his way to fight George Foreman in The Rumble in the Jungle.” He’d flown into Britain without a passport and needed one - much to former boxer David’s delight. As they talked about the sport, Ali said to the photographer: “All those fights and you’re almost as pretty as me!” Ali then ordered multiple prints and autographed them for all the customers in the queue.

View 7 Images Nancy Spungen, pictured on 10 August 1978 (Image: Philip Sharkey)

When he saw David’s wall of fame, he said: “Take all those down and just have one picture of me, I am the greatest!” The studio moved for a final time to new premises nearby in 2014. Business faded and it closed its doors for good in 2019, after the US embassy moved across the Thames to Nine Elms, which Philip describes as the “final nail in the coffin.” Luckily, his book keeps the extraordinary story of the studio alive. In the words of Stephen Fry: “This wonderfully produced memoir vividly brings back to life a vanished time in the capital. Delicious.”

Article continues below

*Passport Photo Service: An Unexpected Archive of Celebrity Portraits by Philip Sharkey is published by Phaidon, £19.95 (Phaidon.com)

News.title: Doctors shut down Donald Trump's dangerous claim that favourite drink 'kills cancer'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Doctors shut down Donald Trump's dangerous claim that favourite drink 'kills cancer'

Donald Trump has sparked concern with his latest unfounded medical claim, with experts warning there's no truth to his bold assertion about one particular type of drink

View 4 Images President Donald Trump reportedly believes that diet soft drinks 'kill cancer', alarming experts (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The US president's bizarre claim has left medical experts reeling. Donald Trump has long been criticised for being secretive over his health while poking fun at others' physical conditions. He's also been challenged for questioning established medical science on the likes of painkillers, autism and vaccines.

‌



And now specialists have dismissed his claim that fizzy drinks 'kill cancer cells'. During a recent episode of Donald Trump Jr's podcast, Triggered with Don Jr., Dr Mehmet Oz said: "Your dad argues that diet soda is good for him because it kills grass - if poured on grass - so, therefore, it must kill cancer cells inside the body."

‌



The former cardiothoracic surgeon continued: "You know, we were on Air Force One the other day, and I walk in there because he wants to talk about something, and he's got an orange soft drink on his desk. He's got a Fanta on the desk. And I say, 'Are you kidding me?’ So he starts to, like, sheepishly grin. He says, 'You know, this stuff's good for me, it kills cancer cells.'"

‌



Donald Trump's most manic health rants as spokesman forced to deny death rumours READ MORE :

View 4 Images Trump is known to be a huge fan of fizzy drinks, even installing a Diet Coke button in the White House (Image: AP)

Coming to his dad's defence, Don Jr., Trump's eldest son, replied: "OK, OK, but then maybe he's onto something. Because I will say this: I know a lot of guys pushing 80 — not a lot have his level of energy, recall, stamina."

But while family members may think Trump is onto something, medical experts do not agree. Umar Razzaq told the Mirror: "As a registered UK pharmacist for over 20 years, I can say clearly that there is no scientific evidence to support the claim that diet or any soft drinks can kill cancer cells in the human body.

‌



"Whilst some drinks are acidic and may damage surfaces like grass, this has no relevance to how cancer develops or is treated in people. Human biology is far more complex, and cancer treatments are based on rigorously tested medicines and therapies approved by the MHRA.

"Claims like this tend to arise from misunderstandings of basic chemistry and how the body works. While diet soft drinks are generally considered safe in moderation, they are not a treatment for cancer and should never be viewed as having any protective or curative effect."

View 4 Images This isn't the first time that POTUS has weighed in on matters of medical science (Image: AP)

‌



Meanwhhile, Dr Andy Gaya, a consultant oncologist from the Cromwell Hospital London, said that while the comments may have been "tongue in cheek," there's absolutely no truth to them. "Your body tightly controls its acid levels (called pH), and drinking soda does not make your body acidic enough to kill cancer cells - your body will regulate the acid levels to prevent this," he explained.

This isn't the first unfounded medical science claim Trump has made. Duing the COVID-19 pandemic, he falsely asserted that "99 per cent" of cases "are totally harmless." To the dismay of health professionals worldwide, Trump publicly proposed a number of unsupported and dangerous treatments for the virus, including the suggestion that injecting disinfectant into a person's body could be effective.

The president has also promoted the widely disproven notion that there is a link between autism and vaccines, even going as far as to suggest he would change the schedule for childhood vaccinations. Misleading comments about abortion healthcare have also caused concern, with POTUS previously claiming that babies were being killed after birth.

‌



But where did this unfounded fizzy drink claim come from? Dr Gaya explained: "Very sugary or very acidic environments can damage or kill cells in the laboratory - including cancer cells. Fizzy drinks contain acids (like citric acid in Fanta, or phosphoric acid in Coke - which can dissolve away teeth) so some people (maybe POTUS) assume that it may have a similar effect in the body - but it's just as likely to kill normal cells as cancer cells".

View 4 Images In an age of widespread misinformation, these sorts of claims cause particular concern (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Trump's comments comes at a concerning time in the fight against harmful misinformation. According to news reliability website NewsGuard, almost half of Americans fell for false online claims in 2025, with AI-generated content playing a significant role in misleading people. A staggering 46 per cent believed in at least one false claim between June and December, with confusion soaring further at times thanks to fake viral clips.

‌



But what sort of impact could Trump's fizzy drink claim actually have, and should we be worried? Dr Tony Banerjee, GP and Founder of HarleyDoc, who has himself recovered from advanced bowel cancer, said: "This is the sort of claim that sounds amusing until you remember how easily misinformation spreads."

"One of the problems with comments like this is that they can make dangerous myths sound plausible. When influential figures speak casually about health, some people will inevitably take those remarks seriously. Cancer is not something that should be trivialised with pub-science logic. If a substance genuinely killed cells indiscriminately in the body, that would raise concerns about toxicity, not prove it is a treatment.

"The public deserves clear, evidence-based health messaging. Soft drinks are not anticancer therapies, and suggesting otherwise risks feeding misinformation at a time when trust in medical advice is already fragile. Even when these comments are made jokingly, they matter. Powerful people shape public understanding, and that comes with a responsibility not to amplify myths that could confuse or mislead patients."

News.title: Blood pressure and heart disease risk for anyone using chlorhexidine
News.content:
Blood pressure and heart disease risk for anyone using chlorhexidine

You need to check the ingredients

View 3 Images A man using mouthwash

Social media videos are claiming that mouthwash can raise the risk of if high blood pressure and heart disease by wiping out “good” bacteria that are important for the cardiovascular system, but an expert says the truth is 'far more complex'.

‌



Our mouths contain a variety of bacteria which help prevent disease, support normal functions and contribute to good health. Joanna L'Heureux, Postdoctoral Researcher in Public Health and Sport Sciences at the University of Exeter, said: "One of the important roles these oral bacteria have is converting the nitrate in our food (typically from sources such as leafy greens) into nitrite. When we swallow nitrite, the body turns it into nitric oxide." She added: "It’s one example of how bacteria contribute to keeping the body healthy."

‌



Nitric oxide plays an essential part in regulating blood pressure and supporting brain function and muscle function.

‌



View 3 Images It depends what type of mouthwash you use

Joanna told The Conversation: "Several small studies have actually found that giving people mouthwash can change the balance of bacteria in the mouth. This may reduce the bacteria’s ability to turn nitrate from vegetables into nitrite, which the body needs to make nitric oxide."

Getting married could save your life, frozen dead man brought back, fruit and veg win Alzheimer's fight, and scientists find 'natural Ozempic' that comes without the annoying side effects - all this and more in our latest science newsletter

‌



But, she added: "The key detail that may be missed out of some of these online social media videos is the type of mouthwash used in these studies. Many of the studies which have found a link between mouthwash use and blood pressure gave participants chlorhexidine.

"This is a strong, over-the-counter antiseptic mouthwash only recommended for short-term use in people with gum disease or after dental procedures where its antimicrobial effects are beneficial. Chlorhexidine disrupts oral bacteria to help with infection control – including the bacteria that convert nitrate into nitrite. This makes it an ideal mouthwash to use for researchers wanting to study the nitrate-nitrite-nitric oxide pathway. However, it also means the findings may not reflect what happens with milder, everyday mouthwashes."

View 3 Images Oral health impacts the rest of your body

‌



A trial with 12 healthy adults investigated the effect of three different mouthwashes (and gargling water, which acted as a control) on oral bacteria.

After drinking a nitrate-rich juice, researchers measured how much nitrate was converted to nitrite by oral bacteria. Water and the mild mouthwash (which didn’t contain harsh ingredients such as chlorhexidine) caused a typical response, where nitrate was converted into nitrite.

But the cetylpyridinium chloride mouthwash (which also has strong, anti-bacterial effects) partially blocked the conversion of nitrate to nitrite. The strongest chlorhexidine mouthwash almost completely stopped this process. This is consistent with their stronger antibacterial effects. The stronger types of mouthwash were also linked to higher systolic blood pressure.

‌



Alcohol (ethanol) is another common ingredient in many mouthwashes. As an antimicrobial, alcohol may influence the oral microbiome.

Joanna said: "However, there are currently no studies that have specifically examined the effects of ethanol-only mouth rinses on the oral microbiome or cardiovascular health.

"Overall, the body of evidence suggests that a mild, over-the-counter mouthwash, like the kind most people buy at stores, may be less likely to significantly interfere with nitrate-to-nitrite conversion or affect blood pressure."

‌



More research needed

She added: "Together, these studies suggest that some types of mouthwash (such as chlorhexidine) disrupt beneficial oral bacteria and the nitrate-nitrite-nitric oxide pathway when used long term. But more research needs to be done to truly understand the long-term effects of other types of mouthwash on cardiovascular health – including mild everyday mouthwash brands and those containing alcohol.

"Mouthwash comes in different types for different purposes, so it’s important to check the active ingredient on the back of the packaging. Alcohol-free and milder mouthwashes appear to have less effect on the heart-healthy bacteria than stronger types.

"However, be aware to check the ingredients as even alcohol-free options can contain antibacterial agents such as cetylpyridinium chloride. As such, it’s best to choose one that fits your needs and use it in moderation. Strong mouthwashes containing chlorhexidine are best reserved for helping gum disease or oral infections.

Article continues below

"It’s also worth noting that oral health and untreated infections can also contribute to heart disease more broadly. For example, a systematic review of 82 studies concluded that chronic oral disease and tooth loss was associated with risk of heart problems. This is why maintaining a healthy balance of mouth bacteria matters beyond your teeth.

"Take care of your oral and overall health by keeping up with brushing, flossing, visiting your dentist and choosing a mouthwash that works for you."

News.title: 'I've met all the senior royals and two things about Andrew made him different'
News.content:
'I've met all the senior royals and two things about Andrew made him different'

Royal expert and author Robert Hardman has opened up about his various encounters with the Royal Family over the past three decades and why Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was always different

View 4 Images Andrew stood out for all the wrong reasons, according to the royal expert (Image: Karwai Tang, WireImagevia Getty Images)

A royal expert has opened up about his various encounters with senior members of the Royal Family — and said two things made Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor stand out from the rest.

‌



The disgraced former prince is now living in Marsh Farm after being booted out of Royal Lodge having lived there since 2003.

‌



Further troubling revelations about his association with paedophile Jeffrey Epstein, along with his arrest in February under suspicion of misconduct in public office, have further cast him astray from his family.

‌



But Robert Hardman, who has now written a new biography about the late Queen Elizabeth II, has said Andrew was always different.

He said his encounters with him were a contrast to what it was like being in the company of his nephews, parents and siblings.

View 4 Images The christening of Princess Eugenie (Image: Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)

‌



Royal commentator and author Robert, 60, who has covered 70 tours from Abu Dhabi to Ukraine, said: “Philip was fascinating and sharp — you really had to keep your wits about you. Ditto Charles. The Princess Royal is fabulous — I've followed her around and could barely keep up. William and Harry can effortlessly work a room, charming everyone and putting them at ease.”

And speaking to the Sunday Telegraph about his dealings with Andrew, he continued: “But Andrew just isn’t as intelligent or as articulate as the others. As trade envoy, he was forever saying disobliging things and putting his foot in it.

“He’d be at a telecoms conference and suddenly come out with the line, ‘What is Orange?’”

‌



View 4 Images The former prince (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Robert’s new biography is called Elizabeth II: In Private. In Public. The Inside story — and it is his sixth book about the royals.

He spoke about the Queen a century after her birth and claimed it was her who first wanted her son to move out of Royal Lodge.

‌



Robert said she “believed him” when he claimed he had cut ties with Epstein before his lies were eventually exposed and King Charles removed the titles he was granted at birth.

As for the Queen not being alive for this, Robert added: “I think one of the blessings in all this is that the Queen wasn't around to live through the final degradation, and the brutal disgrace of a royal having their 'princedom' taken away.”

View 4 Images Robert Hardman (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

The broadcaster and journalist also revealed why the Queen had an “instinctive sympathy” for the “spare” Prince Harry.

He said she “always adored” her grandson and added that her father, who was suddenly led to the throne after the abdication of his brother, was a spare, as was her sister, Margaret, who she often defended.

Robert, who has reported on royals for over 30 years, claimed she was "conscious" that both Harry and Andrew had “clearly less defined roles” simply because they were the second sons.

News.title: Dead bodies of at least 50 babies found dumped in Trinidad and Tobago graveyard
News.content:
Dead bodies of at least 50 babies found dumped in Trinidad and Tobago graveyard

The bodies of at least 50 babies and six adults have been found dumped at a graveyard in Trinidad and Tobago - police have launched an urgent investigation

View 2 Images The remains of at least 50 infants and six adults were discovered at the graveyard (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

An investigation has been launched after the bodies of at least 50 babies and six adults were found dumped in a graveyard.

‌



Police in Trinidad and Tobago said 56 bodies - mainly of infants - were found at one of the country's cemeteries on Saturday.

‌



The twin-island Caribbean nation has been struggling with surging crime, including deadly gang violence, which prompted authorities to extend an existing state of emergency last month.

‌



The gruesome discovery was made at the cemetery in the town of Cumuto on Trinidad, approximately 40km (25 miles) east of the capital, Port of Spain.

According to police, 50 bodies were of infants while the remaining were of four men and two women. Police said five of the adults had toe tags, such as those found in morgues, and that a man's and a woman's body had signs of an autopsy. They did not immediately say if any of the bodies had been identified.

‌



View 2 Images 50 bodies were of infants while the remaining were of four men and two women (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Police said they were working to determine the origin of the human remains and any associated breaches of law or procedure.

"Every cadaver must be handled with dignity and lawful care," police commissioner Allister Guevarro said. "Any individual or institution found to have violated that duty will be held fully accountable." A preliminary investigation shows it may be a case of an "unlawful disposal of unclaimed corpses".

Article continues below

The US state department has issued several travel advisories for Trinidad and Tobago since the state of emergency was issued on March 2, due to crime and "a heightened risk of terrorism".

"Although violent crime in Trinidad and Tobago has dropped greatly since 2024 due to security efforts started during the previous state of emergencies, crime remains a challenge throughout the country," the advisory said.

News.title: Sarah Ferguson 'hasn't abandoned' Andrew and has 'been laying false breadcrumbs'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Sarah Ferguson 'hasn't abandoned' Andrew and has 'been laying false breadcrumbs'

Sarah Ferguson might have been spotted hiding out in Austria to avoid the Epstein scandal, but a royal expert claims there is no chance that Sarah has abandoned Andrew for good

View 2 Images Andrew and Sarah Ferguson have gone their separate ways - for now (Image: Getty)

Sarah Ferguson and Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor have gone their separate ways for the first time in years, but they might not be as estranged as people think.

‌



When Ferguson was spotted in an unnamed Austrian village last week, it was the first time anyone had seen the former duchess for over 200 days. Clearly trying to go unnoticed, she was pictured with her red hair tucked inside a baseball cap as she exited a blacked out car outside a ski chalet she is reported to be staying in - which costs £2,000 a night.

‌



Until February, Sarah and Andrew shared the same home, Royal Lodge, but when King Charles forced his errant younger brother out of the lavish Windsor mansion over his connection to paedophile Jeffrey Epstein, and into a more modest property on the Sandringham Estate, it emerged that Ferguson would not be making the move with him. Despite being divorced for decades, the pair have always remained close, with Sarah long taking on the role of her ex-husband's fiercest defender.

‌



View 2 Images Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor pictured following his arrest (Image: REUTERS)

Andrew was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in a public office on his 66th birthday on February 19, and was released pending further investigation while properties in Berkshire and Norfolk were searched. He has been holed up in Norfolk, barely going outside - reportedly on the orders of his big brother - and answering the door in his dressing gown to receive his weekly supermarket delivery, for months Ferguson has been nowhere to be found.

"She's been laying false breadcrumbs to stop people following her trail, and very few people were allowed in on the secret," a source told the Mirror. "But she's seen Andrew arrested and read all the headlines about the Epstein investigations and knows it's a very grave situation.

‌



Mountbatten-Windsor has faced - and denied - claims that he had sex with Epstein trafficking victim Virginia Guiffre when she was 17. For Ferguson's part, emails released by US Congress as part of the so-called Epstein Files appear to show her begging the late sex offender for money and offering him her support despite publicly denouncing him.

But despite their individual battles and public distance, one royal expert tells The Mirror that behind the scenes, it's likely a different story. Duncan Larcombe, author of 'Prince Harry: the Inside Story' and former royal editor of the Sun, says: "My personal hunch is that it's a public relations move. I don't think she's any nearer ditching Andrew than she ever was and her links to Epstein might have been different from Andrew's but they were still strong. So in other words, it would be pretty... hypocritical if she just said, 'oh how dare you be friends with a man like that' when clearly she's been a friend of the man like that."

Larcombe notes how friends seem willing to stand by Ferguson and help her hide out on their sofas for free, in stark contrast to the radioactive Andrew, from whom everyone appears to be keeping a wide birth. "It's interesting because you have to think of her ex-husband, Andrew, who it looks like the world and his wife are distancing themselves from him," he says.

‌



"I think it's quite interesting to see that she's still got wealthy friends that are prepared to step into the breach and help her out and I think that's what these pictures expose more than anything. She had links to Epstein. She took money off Epstein. There are still huge question marks hanging over her head when it comes to her friendship with Epstein and yet once again she seems to be the freebie queen."

A friend of Sarah's has confirmed to the Mirror that pals have been 'helping her' during the ongoing scandal, and that she feels somewhat 'abandoned' by the House of Windsor, none of whom are said to have contacted her since King Charles stripped Andrew and Sarah of their royal titles and styles last autumn.

‌



"Sarah is living in fear right now. She's not immune to everything that is happening. She realises how serious everything is, and she is not coping with it.

"She is definitely worried about returning home to the UK and is relying on the kindness of friends to help her through the situation. But she knows she can't keep moving around forever. Sarah feels she has been abandoned by the Royal Family and has been treated very unfairly. She is at a complete loss over what to do."

Both Andrew and Sarah have been called upon to testify to the US House Oversight Committee about what they know about Epstein - but with neither US citizens, never of them are obliged to respond to the request, or appear to give evidence.
